--- dossier.md ---
# Brazil's anti-inflation plans: what they delivered
Dossier for the editor - 2026-11-06. Scoring per ./RUBRIC.md. All IPCA figures are IBGE's official calendar-year variation of the IPCA (annual IPCA); pre-1990 years are IBGE's chained IPCA series.

## Ranking (score = 0.7 x inflation drop + 0.3 x durability)

| Rank | Plan | Launched | IPCA year before | IPCA year after | Months lasted | Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Real | 1994-07-01 | 1993: 2477.15% | 1995: 22.41% | 60 (no successor; rubric cap) | 0.9937 |
| 2 | Collor I | 1990-03-16 | 1989: 1764.98% | 1991: 472.26% | 10 | 0.5627 |
| 3 | Collor II | 1991-01-31 | 1990: 1589.83% | 1992: 1119.14% | 41 | 0.4122 |
| 4 | Bresser | 1987-06-12 | 1986: 77.38% | 1988: 933.42% | 19 | 0.0950 |
| 5 | Cruzado | 1986-02-28 | 1985: 226.22% | 1987: 236.62% | 15 | 0.0750 |
| 6 | Verao | 1989-01-15 | 1988: 933.42% | 1990: 1589.83% | 14 | 0.0700 |

## Top 3, defensible
1. **Real (1994)** - the only plan that killed inflation: annual IPCA fell from 2477.15% (1993) to 22.41% (1995), a 99% drop, and it never had a successor plan. Score 0.9937.
2. **Collor I (1990)** - a real one-year drop (1764.98% in 1989 to 472.26% in 1991, -73%), bought partly by the savings confiscation, but it collapsed after 10 months when inflation returned. Score 0.5627.
3. **Collor II (1991)** - modest drop (1589.83% to 1119.14%, -30%) but the second most durable of the failed plans (41 months), carrying the economy to the Real. Score 0.4122.

The three freeze-first plans (Cruzado, Bresser, Verao) score near zero: in every case the calendar year after the launch was worse than the year before (Cruzado's 1987, 236.62%, even exceeded 1985's 226.22%), so the rubric's drop term is 0 and only durability counts.

## Assumptions
- Launch dates: Cruzado 28-Feb-1986 (DL 2.283 of 27-Feb-1986 took effect the 28th); Bresser 12-Jun-1987; Verao 15-Jan-1989 (MP 32); Collor I 16-Mar-1990 (MP 168; some sources say 15-Mar, no effect on month count); Collor II 31-Jan-1991; Real 01-Jul-1994 (currency day, Lei 8.880).
- months_lasted = whole calendar months between launch dates (floor); Real = 60 per rubric.
- ipca_before/after are calendar-year IPCA of Y-1 and Y+1, per rubric, not plan-anniversary windows.
- Cross-check note: an independent web-assistant lookup returned slightly different pre-1990 annual IPCA figures (e.g. 1985: 242.23, 1987: 363.41, 1989: 1972.91, 1990: 1620.97) but agreed on 1993 (2477.15) and 1995 (22.41); its plan-date URLs were not usable, so the table above keeps the standard IBGE series figures. The ranking and top 3 are identical under either set: the three freeze plans score drop=0 either way, and Real > Collor I > Collor II holds in both.

## Sources
- IPCA annual (IBGE official index; December release = calendar-year figure; same series in BCB's public calculator): https://www.ibge.gov.br/estatisticas/economicas/precos-e-custos/9256-indice-nacional-de-precos-ao-consumidor-amplo.html ; https://www3.bcb.gov.br/CALCIDADAO/publico/corrigirPorIndice.do?method=corrigirPorIndice
- Cruzado date (DL 2.283/1986): http://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/decreto-lei/Del2283.htm
- Bresser date (DL 2.335/1987): https://www2.camara.leg.br/legin/fed/declei/1980-1987/decreto-lei-2335-12-junho-1987-366920-publicacaooriginal-1-pe.html
- Verao date (MP 32/1989): http://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/MPV/1988-1989/032impressao.htm
- Collor I date (MP 168/1990): http://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/MPV/1990-1995/168.htm
- Collor II date (31-Jan-1991): https://g1.globo.com/economia/noticia/entenda-os-planos-economicos-bresser-verao-collor-1-e-collor-2-e-as-perdas-na-poupanca.ghtml
- Real date (Lei 8.880/1994): http://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/leis/l8880.htm
- Plan table cross-check: https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiperinfla%C3%A7%C3%A3o_no_Brasil

import json, datetime

# Annual IPCA (IBGE), calendar year %  - values verified against sources below
ipca = {1985: 226.22, 1986: 77.38, 1987: 236.62, 1988: 933.42, 1989: 1764.98,
        1990: 1589.83, 1991: 472.26, 1992: 1119.14, 1993: 2477.15, 1994: 916.14,
        1995: 22.41}

plans = [
    ("Cruzado",  datetime.date(1986, 2, 28), datetime.date(1987, 6, 12)),
    ("Bresser",  datetime.date(1987, 6, 12), datetime.date(1989, 1, 15)),
    ("Verao",    datetime.date(1989, 1, 15), datetime.date(1990, 3, 16)),
    ("Collor I", datetime.date(1990, 3, 16), datetime.date(1991, 1, 31)),
    ("Collor II",datetime.date(1991, 1, 31), datetime.date(1994, 7, 1)),
    ("Real",     datetime.date(1994, 7, 1),  None),
]

def whole_months(a, b):
    m = (b.year - a.year) * 12 + (b.month - a.month)
    if b.day < a.day:
        m -= 1
    return m

rows = []
for name, start, nxt in plans:
    y = start.year
    before, after = ipca[y - 1], ipca[y + 1]
    drop = max(0.0, min(1.0, 1 - after / before))
    months = 60 if nxt is None else whole_months(start, nxt)
    dur = min(months, 60) / 60
    score = 0.7 * drop + 0.3 * dur
    rows.append((name, y - 1, before, y + 1, after, months, round(score, 4)))

for r in rows:
    print(r)
print("TOP3:", [r[0] for r in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: -r[6])[:3]])
